questions.stem: Which structures are contained in the anal triangle of the perineum?
options: The anal canal and ischiorectal fossae
The urethra and external genitalia only
questions.explanation: The anal triangle contains the anal canal and the ischiorectal fossae.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide states that the anal triangle contains the anal canal and ischiorectal fossae.

questions.stem: Which structure is listed as an anterior relation of the anal canal?
questions.explanation: The perineal body and urogenital diaphragm are the stated anterior relations of the anal canal.
questions.sourceEvidence: The relations list names the perineal body and urogenital diaphragm anteriorly.

questions.stem: What is the posterior relation of the anal canal?
questions.explanation: The slide identifies the anococcygeal body as the posterior relation.
questions.sourceEvidence: The relations list gives the anococcygeal body posteriorly.

questions.stem: In which direction does the anal canal pass from the anorectal junction toward the anus?
questions.explanation: The anal canal passes downward and backward from the anorectal junction.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide describes the canal as passing downward and backward.

questions.stem: Which nerve supply is specified for the external anal sphincter?
options: Inferior rectal nerve and perineal branch of S4
questions.explanation: The external sphincter receives the inferior rectal nerve (from the pudendal nerve) and the perineal branch of S4.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide directly names the inferior rectal nerve and S4 perineal branch.

questions.stem: Where does the outer longitudinal smooth-muscle layer of the anal canal descend?
options: Between the internal and external anal sphincters
Between the two layers of the bladder wall
questions.explanation: The outer longitudinal layer continues from the rectum and descends in the interval between the two anal sphincters.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide describes this layer as descending between the internal and external sphincters.

questions.stem: Which epithelial lining characterizes the lower half of the anal canal in the lecture slides?
questions.explanation: The lower half is lined by stratified squamous epithelium and lacks anal columns and valves.
questions.sourceEvidence: The lower-half column specifies stratified squamous epithelium and absence of columns and valves.

questions.stem: Which artery supplies the lower half of the anal canal according to the slides?
questions.explanation: The lower half is supplied by the inferior rectal artery, a branch of the internal pudendal artery.
questions.sourceEvidence: The lower-half arterial supply entry names the inferior rectal artery from the internal pudendal artery.

questions.stem: The inferior rectal vein drains first into which vein, as described in the slides?
questions.explanation: The inferior rectal vein drains into the internal pudendal vein before reaching the internal iliac vein and systemic circulation.
questions.sourceEvidence: The lower-half venous drainage pathway begins with the inferior rectal vein entering the internal pudendal vein.

questions.stem: Which lymph nodes receive lymph from the upper half of the anal canal in the slide table?
options: Superior rectal nodes, then pararectal and inferior mesenteric nodes
Deep inguinal nodes, then external iliac nodes
questions.explanation: The upper-half pathway runs through superior rectal nodes and pararectal nodes to inferior mesenteric nodes.
questions.sourceEvidence: The upper-half lymph entry lists superior rectal nodes, pararectal nodes, and inferior mesenteric nodes in sequence.

questions.stem: What configuration do the puborectalis fibres form around the anorectal junction?
options: A complete circular ring around the anal verge
A straight band between the ischial tuberosities
A V-shaped ligament behind the coccyx
questions.explanation: The puborectalis fibres blend with the deep external sphincter to form a U-shaped sling.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide describes the puborectalis fibres as blending with the deep external sphincter into a U-shaped sling.

questions.stem: Which structures form the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa?
options: Obturator internus, obturator fascia, and pudendal canal
questions.explanation: The lateral wall is formed by obturator internus, its fascia, and the pudendal canal.
questions.sourceEvidence: The boundary list explicitly names obturator internus, obturator fascia, and pudendal canal laterally.

questions.stem: What forms the anterior boundary of the ischiorectal fossa?
options: Superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles
questions.explanation: The anterior boundary is formed by the superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles.
questions.sourceEvidence: The boundary list names the superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles anteriorly.

questions.stem: Which named nerve and vessels are contents of the ischiorectal fossa?
questions.explanation: The fossa contains the inferior rectal nerve and vessels; the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels lie within the pudendal canal.
questions.sourceEvidence: The contents list includes inferior rectal nerve and vessels, followed by pudendal structures within the canal.

options: A splitting of the obturator fascia
A tunnel through the sacrotuberous ligament
A passage through the levator ani
A division of the perineal membrane
questions.explanation: The pudendal canal is a tunnel formed by splitting of the obturator fascia.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide defines the canal as a tunnel formed by splitting of obturator fascia.

questions.stem: Which territory is supplied by the perineal nerve, a branch of the pudendal nerve?
options: Urogenital triangle muscles and skin on the posterior scrotum or labia majora
Lower half of the anal canal and perianal skin only
Levator ani and skin over the sacrum
questions.explanation: The perineal nerve supplies muscles of the urogenital triangle and skin on the posterior scrotum or labia majora.
questions.sourceEvidence: The slide assigns urogenital-triangle muscles and posterior scrotal/labial skin to the perineal nerve.
